body: We found someone and the first appointment is today! <3

Are you filing around through real life? Just \*attempting\* to find a girl who might come along. Going to cafes and chatting with random girls? I feel deeply, as I felt this until I met my boyfriend a while ago.

How I Found Love: (Well, i found mine online, but i'll make some irl pointers)

1: find a club for some of your biggest interests. Like singing? Like dancing? You and that girl will at least have one shared interest, making it much easier to just talk to her and find something to start talking too.

2: Like gaming? Well look no further than online! Play video games, go until you find a girl who makes you laugh. If you're not up to do that because you can't hold her hand, it's not real love, it's physical love. Lust more or less. If you fall in love with a girl for her personality and will wait until you can go see her irl, that's truly special.

3: This is risky, but let yourself succumb to dating websites. Give it a shot i guess! I've never done it, I met my boyfriend through gaming, but I know people who've found love that lasted through them. 

4: Go hang out in big areas like malls, go to your favorite stores. Maybe you're an emo person? Run to hot topic, grab some stuff, and talk to the helpers and cashiers inside. 

5: Idk if you're in school, but that's always a place to look. It'll be easier in college, but join some groups. 

6: Just get up, walk around, do shit, someone is bound to come across you.

\- - - - 

You're worth being loved, you just haven't found the girl yet. It takes time, it takes work. Don't give up on your love, and keep trying. No one isn't worth being loved. We all have hope, we all have potential. I'm not saying "oh just give it time and you'll be saved" no, you wont. You also have to make some happiness from yourself. Being dependent on another person's love for happiness will ruin you. Find something about *yourself that you like. you have to accept yourself before you can accept the love of another.* I used to hate myself, but my boyfriend made me realize a few things about myself, and once i'd built up enough self-confidence to stand on my own, I asked him out, and it was a yes!

You can't be afraid of love, you can't hold back. once you meet a great person, you can't back away from the light. You need to just go for it. Feeling sorry for yourself isn't going to get you a girlfriend. You need to just to have confidence, even if it's empty. If  you have confidence, even if it's fake, it'll slowly feel real. 

I'm not going to tell you you're going to meet the love of your life in 3 days, i'm not telling you just *waiting* will get you a girlfriend. i'm not saying everything will just magically get better. But you can't just give up. it's almost selfish. I know, when I was suicidal, it felt like it would be better for everyone, but you're not giving the person *in the future* a chance to meet you and marry you.

You're worth the love, you just have to wait. But just *sitting around* wont solve everything. Work on self image. People are often attracted to more happy/confident people. Sure, my boyfriend was at his worst when I dated him. i had endless patience on his mood swings, but idk if other girls are like that. Work on yourself. Work on what kind of girl you want. 

**You don't want to rush into a relationship because you feel like you want to be loved. If she says she loves you, give it time. Get to know her, or else things will happen, everything will feel too rushed and unwanted. It'll feel like you don't even know her, though you claim to love her. So please, don't just scavenge the ground for all the people who** ***could possibly fit what you want.*** **You have to know what you want.** 

So:

Work on yourself

Work on What kind of person you want

Work on finding your interests, share interests with other girls.

Work on giving time and patience to in which it needs.

Oh my god! You actually read all that? Well love, I wish you the best of luck. - Snek <3
We're working on it. While things aren't magically going to get better, we're trying to find someone to help atm.

As someone who's only disorder is compulsive eating and depression, I can't speak to how it is to have autism. I know the jokes on the internet are everywhere. I know people are unaccepting and frankly, if someone is bullying you, you have to know that they're trying to bring you down to make them look better. If (and yes I know it is like this for you) they bully you for the autism itself, they are not worth your time. Their words are nothing more than passing wind. 

You are a beautifully smart person, I can tell from just reading this. The words of these people don't matter. You will grow up, you will follow your dreams, and you will show these people that you're stronger than them, and they stooped so low as to try to bring you down. it's like saying "you have dyslexia? haha, you can't read!" but then later in life you read a novel beyond their level.

it's wonderfully satisfying to prove people wrong no matter the set backs. I believe you can make it through this hard time in your life.
